new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the first syllable of the (prefixless) word, i.e. the first syllable of the root; a secondary stress on the third syllable (left-to-right trochaic alternation). Prefixes are unstressed and do not shift the pattern; suffixes and clitics do not move stress. Stress delimits word boundaries.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the third syllable (p. 34); elsewhere (p. 181) summarized as 'Word stress.. would appear on the 1st and 3rd syllable, while prefixes usually are not marked by stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) Words with lexically fixed non-initial stress, mostly loans and place names (märäkhá 'orange', karíj 'hard', farâj 'leave', yoshropái 'thanks', poróma 'before', Köwë'dö 'Covendo') and a few native words; these keep their stress when affixed. (b) 'Flexible' roots (ats- 'come', ay- 'come (F)', tyab- 'fish', cham- 'fish with arrow', khosh- 'sleep', cha- 'go down', kew- 'search', tye- 'pass'; noun eme 'female turkey') take initial stress when bare but second-syllable stress when further derived, yielding minimal pairs such as chabán 'he goes down again' vs. chában 'he vomits again'. Sakel calls word stress '(phonemic)'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (root + affixes/clitics as one phonological word); stress is not written in the orthography except to disambiguate (p. 43). Description is of Mosetén of Covendo; Chimane not separately described for stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement describes Mosetén of Covendo (Sakel 2003 p. 5: 'The present grammar is about the variant Mosetén of Covendo'), one of three variants (Mosetén of Covendo, Mosetén of Santa Ana, Chimane/Tsimane') that Glottolog lumps under mose1249 (no dialect children in the Glottolog JSON). Chimane, the largest variety, is not separately described for stress in any opened source. The file held by the project named Sakel2004 is actually the 2003 Nijmegen thesis (title page says Proefschrift, 19 Feb 2003).

sources.note: Section 2.4 Stress, pp. 34-35 (pdf pp. 63-64): stress generally on the first syllable of the word with secondary stress on the third syllable; prefixes excluded (stress on first root syllable); fixed non-initial stress in loans/place names and a few native words; a small set of roots shift stress to the second syllable under derivation; stress marks word boundaries. Also p. 10 (1.6): 'Word stress generally falls on the first syllable'. Variety = Mosetén of Covendo.
